selected_text: Hypothesis: the strict and permissive pair expressions both use a greedy name class that overlaps following whitespace, so a long whitespace-heavy prefix with no equals sign forces many name/whitespace split attempts and quadratic event-loop CPU use. Prerequisites: read access to the parser source, a local JavaScript runtime, disposable source copies, and untrusted Set-Cookie text reaching the public parse entry point; permissive mode is opt-in and ordinary cookies are available as controls. Bounded test: time parsing 'a'.repeat(n) + ' '.repeat(n) + '!' for n = 2000 through 64000 in both modes with a median of three and a fixed external timeout, compare with a no-whitespace malformed cookie and an early-equals value tail, and add a semicolon-plus-attribute variant to exclude later stages; then replace both pair expressions with a deterministic left-to-right separator scan and re-run the same matrix plus a strict/permissive semantic differential. Expected support: about fourfold growth per doubling before the repair and near-linear growth after, with zero field changes on ordinary, quoted, empty-name, leading and multiple equals, terminator, attribute, and trailing-semicolon cases. Falsifier: before the repair, flat timing or only one mode affected; after the repair, any key, value, or attribute change or more than roughly twofold growth per doubling. Cleanup and limitation: delete disposable fixtures and keep the differential corpus; one input family and one machine do not prove universal equivalence, and a separate attribute-loop sink may remain.
